confirmed_findings: Critical MU 4.9.38 reads yantra-puruṣāḥ; vulgate 4.27.38 reads atyajña-puruṣāḥ.
Uṇādipāṭha 4.166 supplies √yam + tra and explicitly lists यन्त्रम्, without assigning tra fixed semantic force.
Nirukta 2.3 transmits puri ṣādaḥ, puri śayaḥ, and pūrayater vā / pūrayaty antar; English person does not exhaust this inherited field.
Robots is defensible only as a contextual, non-etymological equivalent of the whole yantra-puruṣa expression and not as a replacement for puruṣa.
Swami Venkatesananda's robot-like phrase is modern interpretive reception of the whole construction/automatic-action account, not controlling Sanskrit witness or direct token translation.

The critical record is public-ready because its exact Roman witness remains preserved and the complete Devanāgarī layer is explicitly identified as deterministic site normalization rather than a second witness.
